title: Webb County Weighs $1.22 Million Radio Upgrade for First Responders
excerpt: Webb County is considering replacing aging portable radios used by constables and county investigators, after officials warned outdated equipment could leave first responders with limited coverage in rural parts of the county.
content:
Webb County is considering replacing aging portable radios used by constables and county investigators, after officials warned that outdated, single-band equipment could leave first responders with limited communication and coverage in parts of rural Webb County, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

Motorola Solutions presented county leaders with a proposed $1.22 million upgrade this past week. The quote — $1,216,274.58 for an initial package of 85 radios, including seven years of warranty and services — would replace units that Motorola said are more than a decade beyond the manufacturer's support and could lack the parts, repairs and security updates needed to remain reliable.

Motorola Senior Account Manager Jorge Chavez told commissioners the county currently has a “vast mismatched array” of radios, with some models more than 12 years beyond Motorola's support. The county also operates across different radio frequencies: some existing radios are limited to VHF, while newer county, city and sheriff's systems increasingly use 700/800 MHz technology, and VHF-only radios may not be able to use newer sites, potentially limiting interoperability during major incidents.

Precinct 4 Commissioner Ricardo Jaime said the upgrade could be especially important in rural Webb County, where responders have experienced radio dead zones. “Sometimes, a request is made to ask for medical helicopter assistance,” Jaime said, adding that GPS capabilities could help dispatchers quickly identify responders' locations during crashes, shootings and other emergencies.

The proposed APX Next system also offers GPS location sharing, cellular fallback, Wi-Fi connectivity and over-the-air programming. Commissioners questioned how location data would be shared among agencies, with Motorola saying the system can be configured so visibility is limited by department, supervisor or dispatch authorization.

No purchase was approved. Commissioners instead asked county staff and Motorola to expand the proposal beyond the initial 85 radios and determine whether additional departments should be included before the county considers spending the money. The total could reach roughly 130 radios, including fire, marshal, emergency management, planning, engineering and road and bridge personnel, although a revised price was not presented.

Purchasing Agent Joe Lopez said the request came late in the 2026 fiscal year from the constables, the county attorney's office and the district attorney's office to replace the aging portable radios. Jaime noted the Webb County Fire Department has already purchased eight radios through recent budgets, at roughly $14,000 each, and additional units are still needed.

Commissioners ultimately asked Motorola to work with county purchasing and budget officials to develop a broader proposal before returning to the court.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times, Nov. 17, 2026.
